title: Rash
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with sudden onset petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gum bleeding, and possibly mucosal bleeding in an otherwise well-appearing child. No lymphadenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly, no fever, no bone pain — distinguishes from leukemia. ITP is an autoimmune destruction of platelets (antibodies against GPIIb/IIIa). Often preceded by viral URI or vaccination 1-4 weeks prior. Labs: ISOLATED thrombocytopenia (platelets <100K, often <20K). Normal Hb, normal WBC, normal peripheral smear (except low platelets). Bone marrow biopsy NOT needed in typical childhood ITP. Treatment: most children (>80%) recover spontaneously within 6 months. If platelets >20K and no bleeding → observation only. If <10K or significant bleeding → prednisone 2-4 mg/kg/day or IVIG or anti-D (if Rh+). Avoid IM injections, contact sports, NSAIDs/aspirin.
chief_complaint: Petechiae, purpura, easy bruising in well child

stacks.label: Avoid contact sports, NSAIDs, IM injections
